questions.question: Describe the charging and discharging process of a lithium-ion battery / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Working with diagram can give 5 marks
  • Lithium-ion batteries operate by moving lithium ions between a cathode and anode
  • through an electrolyte, typically using a constant -current/constant-voltage (CC/CV)
  • charge profile and a reverse flow during discharge. During charging, ions move from
  • cathode to anode; during discharge, they move back, creating a flow of electrons
  • that powers devices
  • Charging Process (Storing Energy)
  • • Ion Movement: When a charger is connected, it forces lithium ions to leave the
  • positive cathode (typically Li -metal oxide) and travel through the electrolyte and
  • separator to the negative graphite anode.
  • • Electron Flow: Electrons move through the external circuit from the charger to the
  • anode, balancing the positive charge of the incoming ions.
  • Discharging Process (Releasing Energy)
  • • Ion Movement: When a device is connected, the chemical energy is released, and
  • lithium ions move from the anode back to the cathode through the electrolyte.
  • • Electron Flow: Electrons move from the anode to the cathode through the external
  • circuit, powering the connected load.

questions.question: How does a capacitor filter work in a bridge rectifier circuit? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:

  • into a steadier, smoother DC voltage. Connected in parallel with the load resistor, the
  • capacitor charges to the peak voltage during the diode conduction periods and
  • discharges through the load when the rectifier output drops, effective ly filling in the
  • gaps between pulses.

questions.question: Explain the working of Induction motor / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• An induction motor operates on the principle of electromagnetic induction,
  • converting electrical energy into mechanical energy without any direct electrical
  • connection to the rotating part.
  • Stator: The stationary part producing the rotating magnetic field.
  • ` Rotor: The rotating component, either squirrel-cage or wound, that receives
  • induced current.
  • An induction motor works on the principle of Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic
  • Induction, where a stator creates a rotating magnetic field (RMF) when fed by a
  • three-phase AC supply. This RMF cuts the rotor conductors, inducing an EMF and
  • current, which interacts with the RMF to produce torque and turn the rotor.

questions.question: How do input and output capacitors help improve the performance of a 78XX voltage regulator? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Input and output capacitors are essential for ensuring the stability and performance
  • of a 78XX voltage regulator, primarily by preventing oscillations and managing rapid
  • load changes
  • Input Capacitor
  • Stability & Filter : The input capacitor is primarily used to ensure the regulator
  • remains stable and does not self-oscillate. *
  • • Preventing Oscillation: If the regulator is far from the power source (typically more
  • than 10 inches), the lead inductance can cause the IC to oscillate . A small capacitor
  • (typically 0.33 µF) placed close to the input pin bypasses this inductance.
  • • Filtering Ripple: It acts as a reservoir to smooth out fluctuations or AC ripples from
  • the incoming DC supply, ensuring the regulator receives a "clean" signal to process.
  • Output Capacitor:
  • Transient Response : The output capacitor acts as a local energy buffer for the
  • connected load.
  • • Improved Transient Response: The 78XX is a relatively "slow" regulator from the
  • 1970s and cannot respond instantly to sub -microsecond changes in load current. If a
  • load suddenly demands more current, provides that energy immediately, preventing
  • the output voltage from sagging.
  • • Noise Reduction: It filters out high-frequency noise that may be generated internally
  • by the regulator or externally by the load, resulting in a cleaner DC output
